summary: On paper this one is close: Chicago's best edge is to win through the air (Chicago ranks 4th of 32 in EPA per dropback, +0.26), one of its biggest strengths this season), while Detroit's best counter is to win after the catch (Detroit ranks 6th in YAC over expected per catch, +0.3 yds). Under center, Caleb Williams ranks 4th of 31 in EPA per dropback and Jared Goff ranks 12th; x-factor: Amon-Ra St. Brown gets 30% of Detroit's targets and 32% of its air yards, and his WOPR (0.70) ranks 7th of 121. Chicago's pass defense ranks 11th. The model favors Chicago at 52%, mostly on passing matchup (1.6 pts) and starting QB (0.9 pts).

CHI.detail: Chicago ranks 4th of 32 in EPA per dropback (+0.26), one of its biggest strengths this season.
Chicago's defense ranks 17th in explosive play rate (8.9% allowed). Detroit ranks 2nd (10.0%).
Chicago's defense ranks 20th in EPA per designed run (-0.06 allowed). Detroit ranks 9th (-0.03).

DET.detail: Detroit ranks 6th in YAC over expected per catch (+0.3 yds). Chicago's defense ranks 28th (+0.2 yds allowed).
Detroit's defense ranks 1st in QB hit + sack rate vs 4 or fewer rushers (14% generated). Chicago ranks 3rd (12%).
Detroit ranks 18th in red-zone TD rate (59%). Chicago's defense ranks 8th (56% allowed).
